Examination of Wade Tanner’s truck found:

· A red rag in the toolbox; one end rolled to the width of an exhaust pipe and stiffened with soot. Its fibres match those in the mouth of the victim’s exhaust.

WADE TANNER’S TRUCK — EXAMINATION

On the morning of 14 August 2030, at a rest stop on the I-80/90 in Indiana, lorry driver Earl Gaines (59), working for Lakeshore Freight, was found dead in the bunk of his own cab. The engine had stopped and the fuel tank was empty; the refrigerated trailer’s doors were open and the trailer was empty.

The rest stop cashier Sunny Patel found the body at 06.20. A subcontracted Lakeshore driver, Wade Tanner, had also parked at the rest stop that night. The victim’s last radio contact was with the night dispatcher Bev Hollis.

Indiana — August 2030

Subcontracted driver Wade Tanner was offered ten thousand dollars to stop Earl Gaines, who was taking Container 22’s crates to Newark. On the night of the storm at the rest stop, while Earl slept in his air-conditioned cab, Tanner stuffed the exhaust with a rag, moved the crates into his own trailer and pulled the rag back out before dawn.
